title: Exact-v6 neural regret optimizer dose control
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The zero-argmax-movement smoke was optimizer-underfit: on one frozen first-iteration exact-v6 target corpus, a larger warm optimization dose will materially reduce held-out masked Huber loss and flip at least 5% of held-out greedy actions from the identical passive initialization.
material_change: Collect and serialize eight passive-source root traversals, freeze an 80/20 per-seat split, and train matched 32/128/512-step arms from identical weights and sample-order seeds; select the lowest dose passing held-out loss and movement gates.
baseline: The 32-step iterative smoke ended at losses 190.28/133.91, mean TV near 0.08, and zero greedy argmax flips.
notes: No policy-return evaluation is used for arm selection. Frozen corpus hashes and per-arm checkpoints are required.

Before corpus generation, post-close audit identified the baseline smoke's all-zero hidden initialization as a confound. This control retains seeded random hidden features and zeroes only final output projections plus slot1 bias, preserving exact passive initial actions while restoring state-dependent gradients. No corpus or arm had run before this amendment.

result.summary: A frozen 2,672-target exact-v6 corpus isolated optimizer dose. The live-feature 32-step arm moved argmaxes but reduced held-out loss only about 6.6%; 128 steps reduced both seats by 35.2%/33.5% and passed all gates; 512 fit further, so the lowest-passing rule selected 128.
result.conclusion: First-iteration exact-v6 regret targets are learnable when the passive initializer retains live random hidden features. The prior zero-movement smoke was confounded by full-network zeroing and too little optimization.
result.next_step: Run a small optimizer/buffer-resumable iterative exact-v6 pilot at 128 steps, freeze every iteration, track node growth and held-out target curves, and use one untouched multi-anchor deck panel to determine whether learning improves rather than merely fits.
